references.text: The principle of life for life is established here for the first time: 'Whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed.' This forms the basis for the lex talionis principle.
Repeats the principle of life for life: 'Whoever strikes down a person shall be put to death.' This confirms the law of retaliation from Exodus.
The prohibition against taking ransom for a murderer's life underscores the seriousness of the principle 'life for life'.
Repeats the lex talionis principle: 'life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth.' This is a parallel formulation to Exodus 21:23-24.
Jesus quotes and reinterprets this principle in the Sermon on the Mount: 'You have heard that it was said, Eye for eye and tooth for tooth. But I tell you...'
Both illustrate the same legal principle of retaliation (lex talionis) in the books of Moses, where life is required for life.
The verses constitute a coherent legal provision where the ransom rule (v. 30) qualifies the penalty principle 'life for life' (v. 23).
